Rashi on Keritot 2b:10:1.english: One long ritual impurity - For he did not enter the status of purity.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:11:1.hebrew: אלא שמע מינה כו' - ולהכי תנא מניינא, לאשמועינן דדוקא הוא, ולא תימא רבי היא, וסמי מכאן נזיר:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:11:1.english: Rather, conclude from it, etc. - And for this reason [the Tanna] taught the tally, to teach us that it is precise, and do not say that it is [according to] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and strike [the case of] a nazirite from here.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:12:1.english: And he shall sanctify his head - For a second, pure naziriteship.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:13:1.hebrew: ה' מביאין קרבן עולה ויורד - כלומר, על חמש עבירות מביאין קרבן עולה ויורד, בפ"ב (שם):
Rashi on Keritot 2b:13:1.english: Five bring a sliding-scale offering - That is to say, for five transgressions they bring a sliding-scale offering, in Chapter 2 (ibid.).

Rashi on Keritot 2b:13:2.english: Why do I need the tally? - Let [the mishna] teach: "These [bring a sliding-scale offering]."

Rashi on Keritot 2b:14:1.hebrew: משום דקתני סיפא - בהוריות בפ"ב (דף ח:), ואיירי בהנך ה', וקתני הכי: ״אין ב"ד חייבין על שמיעת הקול ועל בטוי שפתים כו' ונשיא כיוצא בהן״ — נמי דפטור אכל הנך, משום [דלא] שייך בהו קרבן עולה ויורד, ועניות בנשיא לא שכיחא. ״ר"א אומר: נשיא מביא שעיר״ — כדינו בכל המצות שבתורה. ואמרי' בגמ': ״לא אמר ר' אליעזר אלא בטומאת מקדש וקדשיו, הואיל ונאמר בהן כרת כבקבועה״. להכי תנא הכא ה' — לאשמועינן דדוקא נקט: דכל המביא על ה' עבירות הללו אינו מביא קבועה אלא עולה ויורד; ולא תימא: סמי מכאן טומאת מקדש וקדשיו לאוקומה כר' אליעזר, דאמר מביא נשיא עליה קרבן קבועה — אלא אינו מביא קבועה; אלא אי ר' יוסי הגלילי דפטר ליה לגמרי, אי ר' עקיבא ור' שמעון דמחייבו ליה בעולה ויורד — דהיינו כשבה או שעירה, או תורים ובני יונה:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:14:1.english: Because the latter clause teaches - In Horayot, in chapter 2 (8b); and it deals with these five [cases], and teaches thus: “The court is not liable for hearing of the voice, or for an utterance of the lips, etc., and the king is like them” — [meaning] that he too is exempt from all these, because a sliding-scale offering does [not] apply to them, and poverty is not common for a king. “Rabbi Eliezer says: A king brings a he-goat” — according to his law for all the commandments in the Torah. And we say in the Gemara: “Rabbi Eliezer said [this] only regarding defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods, since karet is stated regarding them as in [transgressions requiring] a fixed [offering].” For this reason, [the tanna] taught “five” here — to teach us that he specifically stated [five]: that anyone who brings [an offering] for these five transgressions does not bring a fixed [offering], but rather a sliding-scale [offering]. And do not say: Strike defiling of the Temple and its sacred foods from here to establish [the mishna] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who said that a king brings a fixed offering for it; rather, [the tanna holds that] he does not bring a fixed offering, but rather either [follows] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who exempts him completely, or Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Shimon, who obligate him in a sliding-scale offering — that is, a female lamb or a female goat, or turtledoves and young pigeons.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:16:1.hebrew: שלש עשרה ועשרים וד' - מפרש התם בפרק ד' אבות נזיקין (ב"ק ד:), ולשלם ממיטב כדמפרש התם:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:16:1.english: Thirteen and twenty-four - [These are] explained there in the chapter “Four Primary Categories of Damage” (Bava Kamma 4b), and [that they are obligated] to pay from the best-quality [property], as is explained there.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:16:2.english: An informer - One who informs [against another].

Rashi on Keritot 2b:16:3.hebrew: ומפגל - כהן שפגל בקרבנו של ישראל לאוכלו חוץ לזמנו. דחייב — אינו משלם ממיטב, דהאי היזקא דיבורא בעלמא היא, והיזק שאינו ניכר נינהו:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:16:3.english: And one who renders [an offering] piggul - A priest who rendered an Israelite's offering piggul [with the intent] to eat it beyond its designated time. For [even though] he is liable, he does not pay from the best [quality land], as this damage is mere speech, and they are non-evident damage.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:19:1.hebrew: אחותו - בכלל עריות היתה, דכתיב בהו (ויקרא יח): ונכרתו הנפשות העושות, והדר כתיב בקדושים תהיו: איש אשר יקח את אחותו וגו' ונכרתו לעיני בני עמם:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:19:1.english: His sister - She was included in the general category of forbidden sexual relations, as it is written concerning them (Leviticus 18): “And the souls that commit [them] shall be cut off”; and then it is written in [the passage of] Kedoshim Tiheyu: “If a man takes his sister... and they shall be cut off in the sight of the children of their people.”

Rashi on Keritot 2b:20:1.hebrew: אחותו דפרט בה קרא - כי עביד לה בהדי אינך, ליחייב עלה דידה חדא, ואאידך כולהו חדא. ואי תיבעי לך: אשכחן אחותו דיצאת לחלק, אבל שאר עריות למה יצאו? תריץ: לאשמועינן דאיתנהו במיתת ב"ד — עריות שיצאו דכתי' בהו (שם) מות יומת [יש מהן בסקילה ויש מהן בחנק], ויש מהן דכתיב בהו שריפה. והני דאיתנהו בכרת, מפרש להו ביבמות (דף נד.) דפרט בה קרא, ואחותו דבעי הכא לא מפרש:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:20:1.english: His sister, which the verse detailed - When he commits [the transgression with] her together with the others, let him be liable for her one [sin offering], and for all the others, one [sin offering]. And if you should ask: We have found that his sister was singled out to divide [liability], but why were the other forbidden relationships singled out? Resolve [it]: To teach us that they are [subject] to court-imposed death — [namely,] the forbidden relationships that were singled out [and] regarding which it is written (ibid.) “he shall surely be put to death” [some of them are by stoning and some of them are by strangulation], and there are some of them regarding which “burning” is written. And those that are [subject] to karet, [the Gemara] explains in Yevamot (54b) [why] the verse detailed them; but [regarding] his sister, which is asked here, it does not explain.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:22:1.hebrew: בכלל כל הקדשים - אמור אליהם לדורותיכם כל איש אשר יקרב מכל זרעכם אל הקדשים (ויקרא כב). והאי יקרב ליכא למימר דנגיעה היא ממש, דבנגיעה ליכא נטילת נשמה, כדגרסינן במסכת מכות (דף יד:): מבכל קדש לא תגע, והיינו אכילה ולא נגיעה. והאי יקרב נמי מפרש במסכת מעילה (דף י:) דאינו נגיעה, אלא דבר המוכשר ליקרב. א"ר אלעזר: וכי יש נוגע שהוא חייב? אם כן, למה נאמר אשר יקרב? לומר שאין חייבין עליו עד שיוכשר ליקרב. כלומר, אינו חייב על אכילתו משום טומאה עד שיוכשר ליקרב:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:22:1.english: Included in [the general category of] all holy offerings - “Say to them: Throughout your generations, any man of all your offspring who approaches the holy things...” (Leviticus 22:3). And this [word], “approaches,” cannot be said to mean actual touching, for with [mere] touching there is no taking of life [i.e., excision], as we learn in Tractate Makkot (14b) [regarding the verse]: “She shall touch no hallowed thing” (Leviticus 12:4) — and that means eating, not [mere] touching. And this [word], “approaches,” is also explained in Tractate Me’ilah (10a) as not meaning touching, but rather [referring to] something that has become fit to be offered [on the altar]. Rabbi Elazar said: Is there [anyone who merely] touches who is liable? If so, why does [the verse] state “who approaches”? To say that one is not liable for it until it has become fit to be offered. That is to say, one is not liable for eating it on account of ritual impurity until it has become fit to be offered.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:23:1.hebrew: יצאו קדשי בדק הבית - שאינו ענוש כרת האוכלן בטומאת הגוף. והכא נמי, ליגמר כולהו מאחותו:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:23:1.english: This excludes items consecrated for Temple maintenance - For one who eats them in [a state of] bodily impurity is not punished with karet. And here too, let all of them be derived from [the case of] his sister.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:25:1.hebrew: אשת איש שיש לה היתר בחיי אוסרה - שמתגרשת בגט. הלכך, לא גמרי לה מאחותו, ולא משכחת בה בחטאת בהעלם:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:25:1.english: A married woman, who can become permitted in the lifetime of the one who prohibits her - For she can be divorced with a bill of divorce [get]. Therefore, we do not derive [her case] from [that of] his sister, and you do not find in her case [liability for] a sin offering in [a single] lapse of awareness.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:27:1.hebrew: לדונו בכרת ולא במלקות - והיה מלמד על הכלל כולו, דלית ליה חייבי כריתות שלקו נפטרו מידי כריתתן, באלו הן הלוקין (מכות כג.):
Rashi on Keritot 2b:27:1.english: To judge it with karet and not with lashes - And it teaches about the entire general rule, as he does not hold that those liable to karet who were flogged are exempt from their karet, [as taught] in [the chapter] Elu Hen HaLokin (Makkot 23a).

Rashi on Keritot 2b:28:1.english: And to a woman - It should have written: “And you shall not approach a menstruating woman.”

Rashi on Keritot 2b:29:1.hebrew: ורבנן - דאית להו נפטרו מידי כריתתן, ומפקי כרת דאחותו לחלק:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:29:1.english: And the Rabbis - Who hold that [those liable to karet who were lashed] are exempt from their karet, and [therefore] apply the karet of his sister to separate [liabilities].

Rashi on Keritot 2b:29:2.english: Let them derive [it] from “And to a woman” - To separate [liability].

Rashi on Keritot 2b:29:3.hebrew: על אחותו ועל אחות אביו ועל אחות אמו - דסד"א, הואיל ואיסור חד דאחוה אכולהו, לא נחייב אלא חדא:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:29:3.english: For his sister, and for his father's sister, and for his mother's sister - For you might have thought that since a single prohibition of sisterhood applies to all of them, he should only be liable for one [sin offering].

Rashi on Keritot 2b:30:1.hebrew: הרי שמות וגופים מוחלקין - מואל אשה נפקא, מקראות מוחלקין — דמתלתא קראי נפקי: אחותו, ואחות אביו, ואחות אמו:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:30:1.english: Behold, the categories and bodies are distinct - It is derived from “And unto a woman”; [they are] distinct verses, for they derive from three verses: his sister, his father’s sister, and his mother’s sister.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:32:1.english: From “his sister” in the latter clause [of the verse] - For the verse’s [mention of] karet above also applies to it.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:3:1.hebrew: מחוסרי כפרה - דאינן אוכלים בקדשים עד שיביאו כפרה, ובפ"ב (לקמן כריתות ח:) מפרש להו:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:3:1.english: Those who lack atonement - For they do not eat sacrificial food until they bring [their] atonement [offerings], and in the second chapter (below, Keritot 8b), [the Mishnah] explains them.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:4:1.hebrew: עד שיזרוק הדם - כדמפרש בפ"ב (שם ט.): ככם כגר יהיה — מה אבותיכם לא נכנסו לברית אלא במילה וטבילה והרצאת דמים כו':
Rashi on Keritot 2b:4:1.english: Until [the priest] sprinkles the blood - As is explained in the second chapter (ibid. 9a): “As you are, so shall the stranger be” — just as your ancestors entered the covenant only through circumcision, immersion, and the sprinkling of blood, etc.

Rashi on Keritot 2b:4:2.hebrew: אהכי תנא ארבעה - וכל היכא דתני חושבנא, דוקא קתני, ולא תימא תנא ושייר:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:4:2.english: [It is] for this reason that he taught four - And wherever [the Tanna] teaches a tally, he teaches [it] precisely, and do not say [that] he taught [some] and omitted [others].

Rashi on Keritot 2b:5:1.english: Four bring [an offering] for the intentional [transgression] - It is explained in Chapter 2 (ibid.).

Rashi on Keritot 2b:8:1.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda - Who says below (ibid.).

Rashi on Keritot 2b:8:2.hebrew: נזירות דטהרה - נזיר שנטמא וספר ז' לחזור ולהתחיל ולמנות — נזירות טהרה מז' חיילא. ומשכחת לה דמביא קרבן א' על טומאות הרבה, כגון שנטמא בשביעי וחזר ונטמא בז' — דכיון דבז' טהור הוה, הוו להו ג' טומאות. וקרבן אחת הוא, ולא על כל טומאה וטומאה, משום דבשתי טומאות הראשונות לא יצתה שעה ראויה להביא קרבן, דאין הבאת קרבן אלא בשמיני. הלכך, אינו מביא אלא על האחרונה. להכי נקט תרי זימני נטמא בז', דמהדר אג' טומאות, משום דתנא במתניתין טומאות הרבה:
Rashi on Keritot 2b:8:2.english: Naziriteship of purity - [In the case of] a nazirite who became ritually impure and counted seven [days] to return and begin counting [anew] — the naziriteship of purity takes effect from the seventh [day]. And you find that he brings one offering for several instances of ritual impurity, [in a case] such as where he became ritually impure on the seventh [day] and again became ritually impure on the seventh [day] — for since on the seventh [day] he was pure, these constitute three instances of ritual impurity. And it is [only] one offering, and not [an offering] for each and every instance of ritual impurity, because for the first two instances of ritual impurity, a time fit for bringing an offering had not arrived, as the bringing of an offering is only on the eighth [day]. Therefore, he brings [an offering] only for the last one. For this reason, [the Gemara] stated twice 'became ritually impure on the seventh,' as it sought [to establish a case of] three instances of ritual impurity, because the mishna taught 'several instances of ritual impurity.'
